Document.p: Ports let you import and export goods, steel, ore, coal, and food in exchange for money.

You can choose what to trade by double clicking on the port. This brings up a dialog with boxes to select what to import and what to export. If Import and Export are both checked or both unchecked for a commodity, then that commodity will not be imported or exported. A port will not import or export anything until you check the appropriate box. Local markets supply the city. Ports trade with the outside world.

Due to fluctuation in international supply and demand and politics, sometimes trade of certain commodities can be randomly restricted for many years. When trade is restricted, the corresponding checkbox in the port dialog will appear red. If you have multiple ports in your city, the same trade restrictions apply to all ports.

Importing costs you money and exporting makes you money. The price of large exports are discounted, so you make less money per quantity if you export a lot of a particular commodity. Large imports are not discounted.
Ports must be connected to a river all along the east side.
An active Port provides some technology. Note: Exporters discount large exports.

Ports can import and export a lot of capacity. If you want to restrict the amount that is imported or exported, then consider connecting the port to the rest of your city using a type of transport with less capacity such as road or track or put it in range of a market.
For import or export to occur, 100 labor must be consumed.
If there is both import and export, then .0002 tech is produced, which can sustain up to ~10 tech <100 or ~5 tech >100.

Shipments move half the stored stock (exports) or half the available space (imports), rounded down. The shipment must be at least one fifteenth of the port’s capacity for that commodity. Imports cost 10% more than the base export price at the default tariff and require cash in the treasury.

Red boxes mean foreign trade for that product and direction is closed until the new year. A checked box keeps your order ready to resume. Trade also requires workers and enough cargo to form a shipment. The report separates the latest completed month from this month so far. A zero means there was no reportable trade in that period.
